title: Merge maintenance windows
summary: Collapse overlapping and back-to-back time windows into the fewest possible.
prompt: Teams book maintenance windows on a shared cluster as minute offsets `(Start, End)`, half-open:
a window covers `Start` up to but not including `End`. Before publishing the calendar you want
the fewest windows that cover exactly the same time.
Write `List<(int Start, int End)> Merge(IEnumerable<(int Start, int End)> windows)`:
- The input is in **any order**; the result is sorted by `Start`.
- Windows that overlap **or touch** merge: `(1, 3)` and `(3, 5)` become `(1, 5)`.
- A window inside another disappears into it.
- An empty input gives an empty list.
- A window with `End < Start` is a booking error: throw `ArgumentException`.
starter: List<(int Start, int End)> Merge(IEnumerable<(int Start, int End)> windows)
return new List<(int Start, int End)>();
solution: List<(int Start, int End)> Merge(IEnumerable<(int Start, int End)> windows)
var merged = new List<(int Start, int End)>();
if (end < start) throw new ArgumentException($"window ({start}, {end}) ends before it starts");
template: Dojo.Eq("overlapping windows merge", new List<(int Start, int End)> { (1, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18) }, Merge(new[] { (1, 3), (2, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18) }));
Dojo.Eq("input in any order", new List<(int Start, int End)> { (1, 6), (8, 10) }, Merge(new[] { (8, 10), (2, 6), (1, 3) }));
Dojo.Eq("a window inside another disappears", new List<(int Start, int End)> { (1, 10) }, Merge(new[] { (1, 10), (2, 3), (4, 5) }));
Dojo.Eq("back-to-back windows merge", new List<(int Start, int End)> { (1, 5), (6, 7) }, Merge(new[] { (3, 5), (1, 3), (6, 7) }));
Dojo.Eq("empty input gives an empty list", new List<(int Start, int End)>(), Merge(Array.Empty<(int, int)>()));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("End before Start is rejected", () => Merge(new[] { (1, 2), (5, 4) }));

hints: Sort by `Start` first; then each window can only overlap the last one you kept.
A window joins the previous one when its `Start` is at or before the previous `End` (touching counts).
When joining, the new end is `Math.Max` of both ends: a short window inside a long one must not shrink it.
